sentences.text:
This petition is filed for quashing of FIR No.702/2015 under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC registered at PS Baba Haridas Nagar, Delhi and the proceedings emanating therefrom.
2.
The marriage between petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 was solemnized on 29.01.2012 as per Hindu rites and ceremonies at Delhi.
On 13.03.2014 a male child namely Hardik was born from the said wedlock, who is now in the care and permanent custody of respondent no.2/mother.
Due to temperamental differences since June, 2014 both of them started living separately and on 30.12.2015 on a complaint of respondent no.2, the present FIR was registered.

Various litigations were filed between the parties against each other and ultimately on 16.03.2021 the matter was amicably settled between the parties and the divorce has been granted to them by mutual consent.
In lieu of said settlement the parties have agreed the custody of the child shall remain with respondent no.2.
It is further agreed the parties shall not file any claim/cases against each other or against family members relating to their marriage and they shall bear the respective cost of litigation.

3. The respondent no.2 is present today and has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer and she has no objection in case the FIR is quashed as the matter is settled between them and she has no claim left of whatsoever nature against the petitioners including her permanent alimony,
maintenance (present, past and future), stridhan, dowry articles etc.
The affidavits of parties are on record.
The learned APP for the State also has no objection in case the petition is allowed.

sentences.text: In view of the above, there is no impediment in quashing the present FIR as the matter is settled and it would never entail in conviction of the petitioners herein.
Consequently, FIR No.702/2015 under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC registered at PS Baba Haridas Nagar, Delhi and the proceedings emanating therefrom stands quashed.
Pending application(s), also stands disposed of.
However, this will not affect the rights of the child if he may intend to exercise in future against his father/petitioner no.1.

YOGESH KHANNA, J.
